title: Talking About the Weather
summary: Learn how to ask about the weather and talk about sunny, rainy, or cold days. This lesson helps you start easy conversations every day.

sections.p: When you want to know what the weather is like today, you can ask a simple question. We use 'It is' to talk about the weather. For example, when you look outside and see the sun, you can say 'It is sunny'. It is very easy and people use this every day to start a friendly chat.

ex.mean: Asking what the weather is like now.
There is a lot of sun outside.
Water is falling from the sky.

sections.p: The weather changes a lot. Sometimes it is very hot in the summer, and sometimes it is very cold in the winter. We use 'It is' with these words too. You can also talk about the wind when air moves fast around you.

ex.mean: There is a strong wind blowing.

sections.p: When the sky is grey and covered, we say it is cloudy. In winter countries, water turns into white snow. You can look out your window and describe what you see using these simple words.

ex.mean: You cannot see the sun clearly.

tip: Look out your window every morning and say the weather in English. For example, say 'It is sunny' or 'It is raining'.
